artifacts.summary: Research on adding a WARN-level, blast-radius-driven whole-directory-root and duplicate file_scope declaration check to validate-state.sh, surfaced advisory in commands/task.md Create Task Mode.

memory_candidates.content: In this repo, file_scope is only populated by multi-task creators (/meta Component 4a, /fix-it, /spawn) -- the single-task /task Create Task Mode (commands/task.md) never sets file_scope for the new task. Any 'surface X at task creation' feature targeting /task therefore must scan the whole active_projects[] population post-write, not just the newly created entry's own (always-empty) file_scope.

validate-state.sh base-mode checks (1-7) are all PASS/FAIL only -- zero WARN-level output today. --deep checks (D1-D5) require git history. verify-deploy.sh Gate 10 is validate-state.sh's ONLY existing caller (deploy-time, --deep, exit-code-based pass/fail: 0 passes even with WARNs, only exit 1 = FAIL-level fails the gate). Any new advisory check must use log_warn, never log_fail, or it silently turns pre-existing state.json issues into deploy blockers.

The canonical file_scope overlap predicate (normalize: strip trailing slash; overlap: exact match or directory-prefix ancestor either direction) lives exactly once in scripts/lib/file-scope-overlap.sh, exported as both a bash function scopes_overlap() and a splice-able jq def block FILE_SCOPE_OVERLAP_JQ_DEFS. Every consumer (task-lock.sh, orchestrate-batch-admit.sh) sources or splices this rather than re-deriving it. Any new blast-radius/overlap computation in this codebase must do the same.
